title: Nasi Ayam Kicap
steps: Pat the chicken dry, cut it into 3 cm pieces, and wash hands and utensils after handling the raw poultry.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat for 45 seconds, then brown the chicken for 4 minutes, turning once.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 45 seconds until fragrant without letting the garlic darken.
Add both soy sauces and 120 ml water, scrape the pan, then bring the liquid to a gentle boil.
Reduce to medium-low heat, cover, and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes; stir once so the sauce coats every piece.
Confirm the thickest chicken piece reaches 75 C, uncover and reduce the sauce for 2 minutes, then serve over rice with cucumber and spring onion.
image_alt: A plate of Malaysian nasi ayam kicap with rice and soy-glazed chicken

title: Ayam Percik Kelantan
steps: Blend the lemongrass, chillies, garlic, ginger, tamarind, sugar, salt, and 3 tablespoons coconut milk into a smooth paste.
Reserve one-third of the paste for basting, coat the chicken with the remainder, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 210 C or prepare a covered grill for medium heat; line a tray if using the oven.
Arrange the chicken skin-side up and roast for 18 minutes, then turn and brush with half the reserved paste.
Roast for another 12 minutes, turn again, brush with the remaining paste, and cook for 5 to 8 minutes until lightly charred.
Check the thickest part reaches 75 C and the juices run clear, then rest for 5 minutes before serving.
image_alt: Kelantan-style ayam percik coated in a spiced coconut glaze

title: Nasi Kerabu Ayam
ingredient_quantities: 2 cups cooked blue-pea or plain rice
steps: Season the chicken with turmeric and salt, and keep it separate from the vegetables and cooked rice.
Toast the grated coconut in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring until evenly golden; transfer to a bowl.
Heat the oil over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5 minutes on the first side and 4 minutes on the second.
Lower the heat, cover, and cook for 3 to 5 minutes more until the chicken reaches 75 C, then rest and slice.
Blanch the bean sprouts in boiling water for 30 seconds, drain well, and toss with cucumber, lemongrass, chilli, lime juice, and toasted coconut.
Divide the warm rice between plates, add the herb salad and sliced chicken, and serve immediately so the vegetables remain crisp.
image_alt: Malaysian nasi kerabu served with chicken, herbs, and vegetables

title: Laksa Johor
steps: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water until just al dente according to the packet, drain, and reserve 100 ml cooking water.
Simmer the fish in 500 ml water for 7 to 9 minutes until opaque and easy to flake; lift it out, check for bones, and reserve the stock.
Blend the onion and garlic with 3 tablespoons fish stock, then fry the paste and lemongrass in oil over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Add tamarind, coconut milk, 350 ml reserved fish stock, and the flaked fish; simmer gently for 12 minutes without a hard boil.
Season with salt and add a little pasta water if the gravy is too thick; it should coat the back of a spoon.
Place spaghetti in shallow bowls, ladle over the hot fish gravy, and finish with cucumber immediately before serving.
image_alt: A bowl of Johor laksa with spaghetti and rich fish gravy

title: Penang Char Kway Teow
ingredient_quantities: 1/2 cup Chinese chives, cut into 4 cm pieces
steps: Loosen the rice noodles by hand and mix both soy sauces with the chilli paste before heating the wok.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering, then cook the shrimp for 60 to 90 seconds per side until opaque; remove.
Add the remaining oil and garlic, stir for 20 seconds, then add the noodles and toss over high heat for 90 seconds.
Pour the sauce around the hot edge of the wok, toss for 45 seconds, and push the noodles to one side.
Crack in the eggs, leave for 15 seconds, scramble until softly set, then combine with the noodles, shrimp, bean sprouts, and chives.
Toss for a final 60 seconds until steaming and lightly smoky, then serve immediately while the sprouts remain crisp.
image_alt: Penang-style char kway teow with prawns, egg, and bean sprouts

title: Maggi Goreng Mamak
steps: Boil the noodles for 90 seconds only, drain thoroughly, and toss with half a seasoning packet to prevent over-salting.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and brown the tofu for 3 minutes, turning until two sides are golden.
Add the choy sum stems and tomato and stir-fry for 60 seconds, then push everything to one side.
Crack in the eggs and scramble for 45 seconds until softly set before folding them through the vegetables.
Add noodles, chilli sauce, soy sauce, 80 ml water, and the choy sum leaves; toss over high heat for 2 minutes until evenly coated.
Taste before adding more seasoning, squeeze over lime, and serve immediately while the noodles are springy.
image_alt: A plate of Malaysian mamak-style Maggi goreng noodles

title: Roti Telur Bawang
ingredient_quantities: 2 frozen roti canai or plain flatbreads
1/2 cup warm curry sauce for serving
steps: Thaw the roti until flexible and beat the eggs with onion, chilli, and salt in a small bowl.
Heat a flat pan over medium heat for 2 minutes and brush it with half the oil.
Lay down one roti, cook for 45 seconds, turn it, and spread half the egg mixture over the cooked side.
Fold the four edges inward to enclose the egg, press gently, and cook for 2 minutes until the underside is golden.
Turn carefully and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes until the centre is set with no liquid egg; repeat with the second roti.
Rest for 1 minute, cut into squares, and serve hot with warmed curry sauce.
image_alt: Malaysian roti telur bawang filled with egg and onion

title: Murtabak Ayam
steps: Heat half the oil over medium heat and cook the onion for 3 minutes, then add garlic and curry powder for 30 seconds.
Add minced chicken and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking up lumps, until no pink remains and the meat reaches 75 C; cool for 5 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the cooled chicken mixture and salt; divide the filling into four equal portions.
Place one portion in the centre of each flatbread, fold all four sides over to form a sealed square, and keep the seam underneath.
Brush a flat pan with the remaining oil and cook each parcel over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden.
Check the centre is piping hot and the egg fully set, rest for 2 minutes, then slice and serve with curry or pickled onion.
image_alt: A sliced stuffed murtabak-style flatbread served on a plate

title: Rendang Ayam Cili Api
steps: Blend the chillies, ginger, garlic, turmeric, and 60 ml coconut milk into a smooth paste.
Place the paste in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook for 4 minutes, stirring until fragrant and slightly reduced.
Add the chicken and lemongrass and stir for 5 minutes until the chicken surface is opaque.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, add sugar and salt, and bring only to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered over medium-low heat for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Confirm the chicken reaches 75 C and the sauce no longer looks watery, remove the lemongrass, and rest for 5 minutes before serving.
image_alt: Negeri Sembilan-style chicken rendang with chilli and coconut

title: Ikan Bakar Kicap
steps: Pat the fish dry and check for bones, then mix soy sauce, tamarind, chilli, garlic, ginger, oil, and salt.
Coat both sides of the fish with the marinade and leave for 15 minutes while heating a grill pan to medium-high.
Place the fish presentation-side down and cook without moving for 3 to 4 minutes until clear grill marks form.
Turn with a wide spatula, brush with remaining marinade, and cook for another 3 to 5 minutes depending on thickness.
Check the centre is opaque, flakes easily, and reaches about 63 C; cook 1 minute longer if still translucent.
Rest for 2 minutes, squeeze over lime, and serve immediately with rice and sliced cucumber.
image_alt: Grilled fish glazed with dark soy sauce and chilli

title: Sayur Lodeh
ingredient_quantities: 1 cup long beans, cut into 4 cm pieces
steps: Prepare all vegetables in even pieces and keep the cabbage separate because it cooks faster.
Place water, garlic, turmeric, and lemongrass in a pot and simmer over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add carrot and long beans, cover, and simmer for 6 minutes until they begin to soften.
Add tofu, cabbage, coconut milk, and salt, then stir gently so the tofu remains intact.
Cook uncovered over low heat for 7 to 9 minutes with only small bubbles; do not let the coconut milk boil hard.
Check the carrot is tender but not mushy, remove the lemongrass, adjust salt, and serve hot with rice or compressed rice cakes.
image_alt: A bowl of sayur lodeh vegetables and tofu in coconut broth

title: Cucur Jagung
steps: Pat the corn dry and mix it with flour, spring onion, chilli, onion, and salt until evenly coated.
Beat the egg with 80 ml water, pour it into the corn mixture, and stir just until a thick dropping batter forms.
Heat 1 cm oil in a frying pan over medium heat for 3 minutes; a small drop of batter should sizzle immediately.
Drop heaped tablespoons of batter into the oil without crowding and flatten each fritter to about 1 cm thick.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden and the centre is firm, keeping the oil at a steady medium heat.
Drain on a rack or paper towel for 2 minutes and serve hot; discard oil that smells burnt or has become very dark.
image_alt: Golden corn fritters similar to Malaysian cucur jagung
